The case for privacy

Corporate payment flows now settle on public ledgers, and the founders of the industry are building confidentiality into its base layer.

In this section

  1. Stablecoins on public ledgers5
  2. Buterin and Durov6
  3. Policy has turned7

4

$306B of stablecoins now settles on fully transparent ledgers

That exceeds crypto ETFs, DeFi and tokenised assets combined, and every transfer, balance and counterparty relationship is visible to anyone.

Capital in selected onchain financial products, USD. ETF figures are net assets; tokenised assets are distributed value.

Once an address is linked to a company, its payroll, supplier terms and treasury positions become public record.

Tether and Circle issue 84% of supply, so most activity runs through two contracts any analyst can monitor.

At this scale, confidentiality becomes an operating requirement for corporate treasuries rather than a user preference.

“For users that prioritize privacy, this could become a ‘must-have’ feature.”Zach Pandl, Head of Research, Grayscale, on AI and financial privacy, September 2026

5

Buterin and Durov both treat privacy as core infrastructure, not a feature

The founders of Ethereum and of a messaging app with over a billion users reach the same conclusion from different starting points.

Vitalik Buterin
Co-founder
Ethereum
“Privacy is not about standing apart. It’s about standing together.”Why I support privacy, 14 April 2025
Why it matters
Control over information is power, so privacy protects decentralisation, personal freedom and institutions such as the secret ballot.
Where it belongs
In the protocol itself, covering payments, application activity, chain reads and network-level anonymity.
Current gap
Largely a roadmap, with adoption dependent on wallets and applications implementing it.
Same conclusion
Pavel Durov
Founder and CEO
Telegram, over 1B monthly users
“Telegram would rather exit a market than undermine encryption with backdoors and violate basic human rights.”Telegram channel, 21 April 2025
Why it matters
Encryption protects everyday communication and personal safety, and any access built for authorities is also available to attackers.
Where it belongs
In the product, with no backdoors, even at the cost of withdrawing from a market.
Current gap
Telegram’s default Cloud Chats are not end-to-end encrypted; only Secret Chats are.
ImplicationBoth positions point to privacy embedded at the infrastructure layer from the outset, which favours protocols over standalone privacy applications.

In four years the US moved from sanctioning Tornado Cash to listing a Zcash ETF

Sanctions were lifted, builders returned and institutional capital followed, although developer liability remains unresolved.

Upper axis to scale from mid-2022; lower axis expands March 2025 to October 2026. Developer liability is still open: Roman Storm’s retrial is set for April 2027.

Encrypting amounts is not sufficient on its own, because the network connection can still reveal who is transacting.

8

Markets have paid for privacy only where demand reaches the token

Zcash is held as money and Venice buys back its token with revenue, and both are valued above $1B, while networks without that link are valued in the tens of millions.

Grass and Helium make the same point for network capacity: paying customers and token-level value capture support materially higher valuations.

This report applies the same test to each token in our coverage universe.

Market cap, USD, log scale. CoinGecko and MEXC, 15 October 2026.

Privacy token landscape

The first generation of successful privacy products protected money and DeFi: Zcash for private payments, and Aztec and Umbra for private balances and trading on Ethereum and Solana.

The emerging opportunity is privacy for everyday workflows such as AI, browsing, email and internet access. Venice already serves millions of users, and UR’s network is built to host new operators across VPN, email and AI-agent access.

Ethereum L2 for private smart contracts: confidential balances, state and execution
Private balances, transfers and swaps for Solana assets; deposits and withdrawals stay public
Private AI chat, images and API access on open-source models; prompts are not stored on its servers
Bandwidth and routing marketplace: independent providers carry traffic, validators score performance

~348Ktransactions in 30 days; no user count

Senders pay fees; miners and the development fund are also paid from new issuance

Users pay protocol fees and relayer tips; protocol revenue accrues to the DAO treasury
Users pay subscriptions or API credits, or stake $VVV for a daily share of inference
Customers pay operators; URnetwork's UR Pro subscription is operator revenue, not automatically subnet revenue
Does value reach the token
Monetary asset$ZEC is the money, the fee and the mining reward, with a fixed cap. The bet is demand to hold
Fee + stake$AZTEC funds fees, staking and governance; congestion fees burn, the rest pays operators
Governance$UMBRA governs the treasury via MetaDAO markets; no automatic buyback or dividend

Zcash’s valuation reflects demand for the option of privacy rather than its current use

The shielded share of supply rose through 2025 before retreating in 2026.

ZEC trades at roughly twice Monero’s market value and is held in a US-listed ETF, yet most network activity still settles on the transparent side.

Investors are paying for optionality on private use that has yet to materialise at scale.

12

Aztec’s sequencers have staked $12M to secure only $58K of user funds

Aztec’s token design is among the most complete in the group, but usage has yet to arrive and the current release carries a disclosed critical vulnerability.

What it sellsPrivate smart contracts on Ethereum: confidential balances, state and execution, written in Noir.
How value reaches the tokenFees are paid in AZTEC, congestion fees burn, and sequencers must stake 200,000 AZTEC to produce blocks.
What has to be truev6 closes the proving bug disclosed on 7 August, and apps bring user funds well above today’s $58K.
Supply riskOnly 29% is circulating, the Foundation unlocks on 13 November, and governance can mint up to 20% of supply a year.

Price $0.020 and supply 10.35B (CoinDesk, 14 October 2026); circulating supply and unlocks (Tokenomist); staking, value secured and minting limit (L2BEAT, 16 October 2026); vulnerability notice (Aztec, 7 August 2026).

13

Umbra ties team vesting to price targets, but holders have no direct claim on fees

Umbra sells private balances, transfers and swaps on Solana, and its token governs a treasury rather than collecting fees.

What it sellsA private wallet for Solana assets with screening and viewing keys; Nimbus, its network for other apps, is coming soon.
How value reaches the tokenFees go to a DAO treasury that UMBRA holders steer through MetaDAO markets. There is no automatic buyback or dividend.
Why the vesting mattersTeam and adviser tokens unlock only when fully diluted value reaches 2x, 4x, 8x, 16x and 32x the $0.30 sale price.
What has to be trueNimbus brings other apps onto Umbra and deposits grow well beyond today’s $187K.

Price, market cap $5.2M, fully diluted $10.2M and deposits (DefiLlama, 15 October 2026); sale terms (MetaDAO; The Block, 10 October 2025); vesting (Blockworks token transparency filing, 29 September 2026). Not the Ethereum stealth-address project of the same name.

14

Venice is the only token we cover that uses customer revenue to buy back its own supply

Venice sells private AI chat and API access. Paying users fund VVV buybacks, while annual issuance has been cut from 14M to 2M tokens.

New VVV issued per year

What it sellsPrivate AI chat, images and API access on open-source models. Prompts are encrypted on the device and not stored on Venice’s servers.
How value reaches the tokenStaked VVV earns a daily share of inference capacity and mints DIEM, worth $1 of API credit a day. $5 of every $100 of credit purchases buys and burns VVV.
Evidence of demand3.5M registered users and a $100M annualised revenue run rate (company-reported, August 2026), after a $65M Series A at a $1B valuation led by Dragonfly.
What has to be trueRevenue keeps growing so buybacks outpace the remaining issuance, and holdings become less concentrated than today’s top wallets.

Market cap about $1.1B and price about $23 (CoinGecko, mid-October 2026). Issuance: Decrypt, 21 September 2026; Phemex, 19 August 2026. Users and run rate: Erik Voorhees via Phemex, August 2026. Series A: TechCrunch via AI Weekly, 1 July 2026.

19

Every new operator on UR becomes a structural buyer of SN25

Once deposits are priced, operators must acquire and lock SN25 in proportion to the users and data they serve.

Above the dotted line, operators buy more SN25 than miners receive in emissions.

Deposits sit in a reserve that never pays out, so every unit purchased leaves circulating supply permanently. Where the line sits depends on the reference rate UR sets.

Illustrative, not a forecast. The deposit rate is set at zero for the launch period and UR has not yet set prices. Mechanism: UR SN25 architecture (September 2026); UR Foundation SN25 repository.

20

At Helium’s valuation SN25 would be a 10x, and at Grass’s a 58x

URnetwork already reports about 350K monthly users, yet SN25 is valued at $8.4M, below both comparable networks whose customers pay for capacity.

A wide valuation gapTransaction-privacy assets are valued at about $31B, against roughly $46M for the five network-privacy tokens we track, a gap of around 670 times.
A product already in marketURnetwork, the VPN that SN25 supplies, reports about 350K monthly users and 126,717 providers across 103 countries, so the thesis does not depend on a product launch.
Demand linked to usageOnce the deposit rate rises above zero, operators must acquire and permanently lock UR in proportion to their traffic, converting customer growth into token demand. Until then, TAO inflows fund supply.

How value reaches SN25, most likely first

1
TAO inflowsBittensor sets each subnet's emissions by its net TAO inflows over about three months, so staking into SN25 lifts emissions and alpha demand.
Live since November 2025
2
Sector re-ratingSN25 trades as Bittensor's privacy exposure while capital rotates into the category.
Live
3
Operator depositsOperators acquire UR to deposit against traffic, and deposits stay in the reserve rather than returning to circulation.
Rate set to zero at launch
4
Reserve governanceFuture onchain governance could direct how the reserve is used.
Speculative; no proposal

Ranked by likelihood. The deposit pathway is the one that turns UR from a subsidised network into a paid one.

Every operator draws on the same miner fleet, so new demand arrives without new supply cost.

AI agents are routinely blocked by bot controls and data-centre IP detection, and residential routes are what let them reach the open web.

That makes agents a natural second wave of operators after consumer privacy apps, each one buying and locking SN25 for the traffic it serves.

A single linked address exposes a company’s payroll, supplier terms and treasury activity to its competitors

An illustrative month of stablecoin payments at a fictional company, as a competitor would see it.

Corporates do not need secrecy from auditors or regulators; they need control over who can read their records.

Under controlled disclosure the network still verifies every payment, while the amounts and counterparties are visible only to the company, its auditor and its regulators.

28

AI lowers the cost of surveilling public ledgers while raising the value of the data they expose

Both forces increase the cost of operating in public.

“For users that prioritize privacy, this could become a ‘must-have’ feature.”Zach Pandl, Head of Research, Grayscale, September 2026

Grayscale’s view is that AI adoption will lift demand for financial privacy.

Force one

Exposure gets cheaper

Models parse transaction histories at a scale that once took analysts weeks, so watching a public ledger costs close to nothing.

Force two

Private data gets more valuable

Useful assistants need email, records and preferences to work, so people and companies disclose more to them.

Nym offers stronger anonymity guarantees, so UR must compete on network reach and price

UR’s central challenge is establishing who pays for its supply.

Nym combines stronger anonymity with its own VPN, so UR is better positioned as a complement than as a replacement.
